html:
Óc Eo is an archaeological site in the Mekong delta in southern Vietnam, once a busy port of the kingdom of Funan. It flourished from roughly the first to the sixth centuries CE. It may be the port that Greek and Roman geographers called Cattigara.

The French archaeologist Louis Malleret dug there in 1944 and found a walled town laid out with canals that linked it to the sea and to the city of Angkor Borei inland. The finds show how far its trade reached:

  • Roman gold coins and medals, including one of Antoninus Pius from the mid 100s CE.
  • Indian style seals, jewellery and statues of Hindu and Buddhist gods.
  • Chinese bronze mirrors from the Han period.

Óc Eo sat on the sea route between India and China, where ships waited for the monsoon winds to turn. It declined as Funan gave way to inland Khmer states and the route shifted south toward Srivijaya.
